title: The 8 Best Woodworking Squares 2026
metaDescription: Our 8 picks for woodworking squares 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at woodworking squares 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Starrett 11H-12-4R Steel Combination Square with Square Head
products.blurb: Key specs: 12-inch blade, Precision ground, Hardened blade.
strengths: Starrett precision ground blades are calibrated to 0.001-inch accuracy -- the industry standard for precision measurement
Combination square checks 90 and 45 degrees, acts as a depth gauge, and scribes lines with the built-in scriber
Hardened blade resists wear and remains accurate through decades of shop use
The reference recommendation from every serious hand tool woodworker
limitations: Very high price for a combination square
Overkill for basic woodworking where 0.001-inch accuracy is not required
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Woodpeckers Mini Square, Made in USA
products.blurb: Key specs: Machined aluminum body, Calibrated at 90 degrees, American manufactured.
strengths: Woodpeckers machines their tools to the highest tolerances in the consumer woodworking market
Machined to verified 90-degree accuracy -- not just nominally square
American manufactured with dimensional accuracy verified by calibration
Compact size fits in an apron pocket for setup checks and cutting-edge verification at the machine
limitations: High price for a small square
Single angle (90 degrees only) -- does not also check 45 degrees like a combination square

products.name: Empire Level E2994 7-Inch High Definition Rafter Square
products.blurb: Key specs: 7-inch aluminum, 45 and 90 degree, Degree markings.
strengths: Speed square guides circular saws and jigsaws at 90 and 45 degrees -- hooks over the edge of the board
Degree markings around the hypotenuse allow marking at any angle from 0 to 90 degrees
The most versatile and most-used square on a job site or in a shop for basic layout
Lowest price of any quality square -- a tool every woodworker and carpenter owns
limitations: Cast aluminum -- not as precise as machined tools
Not appropriate for verifying tool setups or jig calibration

products.name: SWANSON Tool Co S0101 7 Inch Speed Square, Blue
products.blurb: Key specs: Swanson design (original speed square patent), 7-inch aluminum, Degree markings.
strengths: Swanson is the company that invented and patented the triangular speed square -- the original
Hip and valley rafter tables on the square are the most accurate of any speed square
Slightly higher precision than Empire Level due to Swanson's more careful casting
The professional choice among framers and carpenters
limitations: Slightly more expensive than Empire Level for similar function
Hip and valley scale is not relevant for most furniture woodworking

products.name: iGaging 4-Inch Precision Double Square
products.blurb: Key specs: 4-inch hardened steel blade, Double square (90 and 45 degree references), Machined cast body.
strengths: Significantly more accurate than hardware store try squares at a modest price premium
Machined cast body with a hardened, graduated blade for both marking and reference checks
Compact 4-inch size is easy to carry in an apron and use at the bench
The correct budget precision square before the woodworker is ready to invest in Starrett
limitations: Less precise than Starrett or Woodpeckers
Small blade length limits use on larger panel layout
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Shinwa Sokutei Angle Scribing Square 62081
products.blurb: Key specs: Japanese manufactured stainless steel, Triangular scribing square, High accuracy.
strengths: Japanese manufacturing produces reference accuracy close to Starrett at a lower price
Stainless steel body resists corrosion better than plain steel squares
90 and 45 degree edges are well-calibrated for cut-line scribing and stock squaring
The practical Starrett alternative for woodworkers who want precision without the Starrett price
limitations: Less widely available than Starrett in North America
No sliding head or depth-gauge function like a true combination square

products.name: IRWIN Tools Combination Square, ABS-Body, Blue, 12-Inch (1794470)
products.blurb: Key specs: 12-inch blade, Combination square, Mid-range price.
strengths: 12-inch combination square at an accessible price -- the most practical all-rounder for general woodworking
Adequate accuracy for furniture and cabinet work that does not require calibration-level precision
Widely available at hardware stores for quick replacement
The correct starting combination square before upgrading to Shinwa or Starrett
limitations: Less precise than Shinwa or Starrett
Head-lock can slip under heavy use
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Swanson Tool Co TS149 9 inch Sliding T-Bevel with Brass Bound Hardwood Handle
products.blurb: Key specs: Adjustable angle, Brass thumbscrew lock, Brass-bound hardwood handle.
strengths: Adjustable to any angle -- set from a protractor, transfer to wood, or copy from an existing joint
Brass thumbscrew lock holds the blade securely once set
Brass-bound hardwood handle resists wear and looks traditional
The correct tool for dovetail layout, angled tenons, and any joinery not at 90 or 45 degrees
limitations: Not a square -- does not verify 90 degrees
A specialized tool that complements rather than replaces a combination square
features: Stainless steel blade with inch/metric marks

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
